Shanghai Municipal Police.
（印：整 4 / 3/22）
FILED
Central Station.
August □□, 192□.
REPORT ON New Russian Magazine.
Made by D.I. Sullivan Forwarded by [签名] Director of Criminal Intelligence.
Sir,
A new fortnightly magazine entitled "□□□□□"
(Outside Russia) was on sale on the morning of August □□
The editor is D. Belkin, a Russian, formerly of the
Russian Echo. The publishers are P. Cherkas, formerly
of the defunct "Russian Thought", P. Areenikoff, of the
 Russo-Asiatic Bank, and D. Belkin. The offices of the
paper are at 6 Mission Lodge Terrace, Chapel, Colo.
The contents of the first number are:-
Editorial "about the press"
(2) Short story "The Stranger" by Belvich.
(3) An article by P. Cherkas entitled "An Connoisseur who
became clever".
(4) A funny story entitled "What do I like" by Averchenko.
(5) A funny story entitled "The effect of heat" by
"Wanderer".
(6) Poetry entitled "Solitude" by P. Cherkas.
(7) A funny story entitled "From the notebook of a journalist
Secretary to a Minister.
(8) A funny story entitled "The gift of the Mikado" by
"Bompall".
(9) "Shanghai Girls" by "A"
(10) A political article entitled "at home and abroad" by
B. K.
(11) A critique of a Russian book entitled "New Russian
Book" published in Berlin, by "C"
There is not much of a political nature in the

（印：整 4 / 3/22）
已归档
中央捕房。
192□年8月□□日。
关于新俄文杂志《□□□□□》的报告。
由情报主任 D.I. Sullivan 制作，经 [签名] 刑事情报处处长转呈。

先生：

一份名为《□□□□□》（域外俄罗斯）的新半月刊于8月□□日上午发售。
编辑为俄国人 D. Belkin，此前供职于《俄罗斯回声报》。出版人为 P. Cherkas（此前供职于已停刊的《俄罗斯思想报》）、亚细亚银行（Russo-Asiatic Bank）的 P. Areenikoff 以及 D. Belkin。报社地址位于 Chapel, Colo. Mission Lodge Terrace 6号。

第一期内容如下：
(1) 社论：“论新闻界”
(2) 短篇小说：“陌生人”，作者 Belvich。
(3) P. Cherkas 撰写的文章：“变得聪明的鉴赏家”。
(4) 幽默故事：“我喜欢什么”，作者 Averchenko。
(5) 幽默故事：“热的效应”，作者“Wanderer”。
(6) 诗歌：“孤独”，作者 P. Cherkas。
(7) 幽默故事：“一位部长秘书记者的笔记”。
(8) 幽默故事：“天皇的礼物”，作者“Bompall”。
(9) “上海女孩”，作者“A”
(10) 政治文章：“国内外”，作者 B. K.
(11) 对柏林出版的俄文书籍“新书”的书评，作者“C”

该刊物中政治性质的内容不多，

16/8/22

"Za Rubejom"
(Outside Russia)
15-3-1922.

A leading article is entitled "Something about the Press, which may be summarized as follows:
1. A newspaper should be self-supporting, i.e. should derive its income from subscriptions, advertisements and sales, and not look for any subsidy, otherwise it becomes mercenary.
2. It must be impartial.
3. The conditions of life at present, opinions and social doctrines may be changed and the journalist can only watch and contemplate events, generalize them and deduce conclusions or make hypotheses; and he must be led by one principle: love of our neighbours.
4. The ideals of a journalist are to put down enmity, hatred and extirpation. There is still enough evil in the world. We must fight against it, deprive it of the power and possibility to do harm, but we must first defeat this evil in ourselves. It is true that all the negative qualities have been concentrated in Bolshevism, but are the non-Bolsheviks all good? These are the questions worth thinking over, particularly by those who devote themselves to public activities. The task of the contemporary journalist is not to excite the passions, but to calm and pacify them; not to call to the rough fighting, but to find other ways to the victory of morality. Present history has indicated that on struggling against any violation by force we evoke much worse developments of this violation. This way appears to be false and it must be abandoned. Time and events will show. It is necessary to prepare ourselves to these events cleansing our souls and hearts. This is the only way to salvation and regeneration.
5. The journalist must try to make clear to themselves and others the faults and sins of the past which have been the cause of our misfortunes to-day. We can easily see that we have not lived by love, and at the present time we are living by hatred.
6. We do not know whether we can dream of such great actions, or be successful, but we must think only of use and intention to good and verity. At least we must not assist the dangerous fire to increase. In the pages of our magazine we shall be interested with life and its manifestations we shall look for everything bright and interesting in this life, and we shall remain indifferent to the trivial interests considering only the public good.

4694
1922年8月16日

《Za Rubejom》
（域外俄罗斯）
1922年3月15日。

一篇题为“关于新闻界的一些事”的社论，其摘要如下：
1. 报纸应当自负盈亏，即其收入应来自订阅、广告和销售，而不应寻求任何补贴，否则就会变得唯利是图。
2. 它必须保持公正。
3. 目前的生活状况、观点和社会学说可能会发生变化，记者只能观察和审视事件，对其进行概括并得出结论或提出假设；他必须遵循一个原则：爱我们的邻人。
4. 记者的理想是消除敌意、仇恨和灭绝行为。世界上仍有足够的邪恶。我们必须与之斗争，剥夺其造成伤害的能力和可能性，但我们首先必须战胜自己内心的这种邪恶。诚然，所有负面品质都集中在布尔什维主义身上，但非布尔什维克就都是好的吗？这些问题值得思考，特别是对于那些投身于公共活动的人而言。当代记者的任务不是煽动激情，而是平息和安抚它们；不是号召粗暴的争斗，而是寻找其他途径以实现道德的胜利。近期的历史表明，在对抗任何暴力违犯行为时，我们引发了该违犯行为更恶劣的发展。这条道路似乎是错误的，必须予以放弃。时间和事件将证明这一点。我们需要净化灵魂和心灵，为这些事件做好准备。这是获得救赎和新生的唯一途径。
5. 记者必须努力向自己和他人阐明过去的错误和罪孽，这些正是导致我们今天不幸的原因。我们可以清楚地看到，我们过去并非依靠爱而生活，而现在我们正依靠仇恨而生活。
6. 我们不知道是否能梦想取得如此伟大的成就，或者能否成功，但我们必须只考虑有益之处以及向善和求真的意图。至少，我们不能助长危险的火势蔓延。在我们杂志的版面上，我们将关注生活及其表现形式，我们将寻找生活中一切光明和有趣的事物，而对于琐碎的利益我们将保持冷漠，只考虑公共利益。
